question: Why are the words of a soprano singing very high notes so hard to make out, even in a good hall?
answer: Because high notes leave no room for vowels. A vowel is recognised by resonances of the mouth, the first lying roughly between 300 and 800 Hz. A note near 1,000 Hz has no energy down there for those resonances to shape. Sopranos tune their mouths to the note instead, trading the vowel for loudness.
move: When a signal carries two messages, pushing one to its limit can erase the other.
ask: When I push hard to be heard, what part of my message am I losing?
reference: Joliveau, Smith & Wolfe, Tuning of vocal tract resonance by sopranos, Nature, 2004
